_note: Audited JAMB Economics starter bank. 33 items come from the 2017 and 2018 papers: every key was checked against the economics, and stems/options were rewritten where the source parse fused them. 21 authored items fill the topics those papers do not reach, so every topic has at least four questions. Defective rows and wrong keys were rejected, not guessed; they are recorded in docs/deferred.md.
subject: economics

questions.question: The occupational distribution of a population is mainly influenced by ______.
questions.explanation: Occupational distribution reflects the structure of the economy — the mix of agriculture, industry and services — so economic factors such as the level of development, technology and income dominate.

questions.question: In a capitalist economy, the factors of production are owned and controlled by ______.
questions.explanation: A capitalist (free-enterprise) economy leaves land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship in private hands. Government ownership of the factors of production is a feature of a centrally planned economy.

questions.question: The establishment of industries in rural areas will help to reduce ______.
questions.explanation: Rural industries create jobs and income where people already live, reducing the pressure to move from villages to cities.

questions.question: The number of people who are qualified to work and who offer themselves for employment is called the ______.
questions.explanation: The working population, or labour force, consists of people of working age who are able and willing to work.

questions.question: In which business unit are the owners usually also the customers?
questions.explanation: A co-operative is owned and controlled by its members, who are usually also its customers; any surplus is shared among them.

questions.question: The formula (index of export prices ÷ index of import prices) × 100 is used to measure the ______.
questions.explanation: The ratio of export prices to import prices is the commodity terms of trade. A rise means a country obtains more imports for the same quantity of exports.

questions.question: Which of the following is an invisible item in international trade?
questions.explanation: Invisible trade covers services such as banking, shipping, insurance and tourism. Petroleum, rice and milk are visible goods.

questions.question: The main concern of economists is to ______.

options.text: redistribute income between the rich and the poor
allocate scarce resources to satisfy human wants

questions.explanation: Economics studies how scarce resources are allocated among competing wants. Wants are unlimited, so satisfying all of them is impossible.

questions.question: Productive resources can also be called ______.
questions.explanation: Land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship are the factors of production — the productive resources used to make goods and services.

questions.question: The study of Economics becomes necessary because of the ______.

options.text: large population size of the world
opportunity cost of goods and services
need to satisfy every desire of man

questions.explanation: Scarcity — limited resources against unlimited wants — is the fundamental economic problem that makes choice, and therefore Economics, necessary.

questions.question: The type of demand that exists between a torchlight and its battery is ______.
questions.explanation: Goods used together to satisfy one want are in joint, or complementary, demand: a torchlight is useless without a battery.

questions.question: The principle of comparative cost advantage was propounded by ______.
questions.explanation: David Ricardo showed that countries gain from specialising in goods where their opportunity cost is lower, even if one country is more efficient at everything.

questions.question: The rate at which a country's exports are exchanged for its imports is called the ______.
questions.explanation: The terms of trade express export prices relative to import prices. An improvement means exports now buy more imports.

questions.question: The efficiency of labour is determined by all of the following except ______.
questions.explanation: Efficiency depends on skill, health, motivation and working conditions. A larger population does not by itself make each worker more productive.

questions.question: A situation in which a commodity is sold abroad below its cost of production in the home country is known as ______.
questions.explanation: Dumping is selling exports below home cost or below the home price, often to clear surplus or drive competitors out of a foreign market.

questions.question: The most important function of agriculture to the Nigerian economy is ______.
questions.explanation: Agriculture supplies most of Nigeria’s food and employs a large share of the population, so food security is its most direct contribution.

questions.question: Given that Qd = 15 − 2P and Qs = 5 + 3P, the equilibrium price is ______.
questions.explanation: Set Qd = Qs: 15 − 2P = 5 + 3P, so 10 = 5P and P = 2.

questions.question: One of the basic features of a monopoly is ______.

options.text: the ability to control either price or output
perfect mobility of factors of production
a large number of buyers and sellers

questions.explanation: A monopolist is the sole seller, so it can set price or output because no close substitute exists. A large number of buyers and sellers describes perfect competition.

questions.question: The major advantage of a public limited liability company over a private limited liability company is ______.
questions.explanation: Shares of a public limited company are freely transferable and traded on the stock exchange, while a private company restricts transfer. Limited liability and separate personality apply to both.

questions.question: The main activity in the upstream oil sector in Nigeria is ______.
questions.explanation: Upstream operations cover exploration and extraction of crude oil. Refining, distribution and marketing are downstream activities.

questions.question: The study of the age structure of a population is important because it ______.

options.text: provides the government with statistics on the size of the labour force
provides the government with statistics on the prevailing interest rate

questions.explanation: Age structure shows how many people fall in working ages, which helps government plan employment, education and social services.

questions.question: If palm oil is demanded both for soap production and for cooking, the demand is said to be ______.
questions.explanation: Composite demand arises when one commodity is wanted for several different uses. An increase in one use raises its price and reduces availability for the others.

questions.question: The institution established to enhance Nigeria's exports is the ______.
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Export Promotion Council was set up to promote and develop exports. NEXIM Bank finances trade, but promoting exports is NEPC’s mandate.

questions.question: The reward for capital as a factor of production is ______.
questions.explanation: Land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest and the entrepreneur earns profit.

questions.question: The type of inflation that arises from excess demand over supply is ______.
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand grows faster than output, pulling prices up.

questions.question: Foreign exchange control in Nigeria is administered by the ______.
questions.explanation: The CBN manages the country’s external reserves and administers exchange-control regulations; banks act as authorised dealers under its rules.

questions.question: Given Qd = 30 − 3P and Qs = 9P − 18, the equilibrium quantity is ______.
questions.explanation: Equilibrium requires 30 − 3P = 9P − 18, so 48 = 12P and P = 4. Then Q = 30 − 3(4) = 18.

questions.question: In Nigeria, industrial development can be enhanced by ______.

options.text: ensuring stable prices for manufactured goods
reducing government expenditure on imported goods

questions.explanation: Reliable power, transport and water lower production costs and attract investment. High interest rates discourage investment.

questions.question: All of the following are sources of government revenue except ______.

options.text: personal income, disposable income and transfer earnings

questions.explanation: Personal income and transfer earnings are received by individuals, not by government. Taxes, state earnings, grants and borrowing are government revenue.

questions.question: One of the important qualities that money must possess is ______.
questions.explanation: Money must be homogeneous so that every unit is identical and can be counted and valued. Heterogeneity would make exchange difficult.

questions.question: One of the functions of money deposit banks in economic development is ______.

options.text: acting as banker to the government

questions.explanation: Deposit money banks mobilise savings and lend to households and firms. Being banker to government, making monetary policy and issuing currency are CBN functions.

questions.question: One of the arguments against the practice of monopoly is ______.
questions.explanation: A monopolist faces no competitive pressure and may charge high prices, restrict output and exploit consumers.

questions.question: A well-conducted census is important for ______.

options.text: providing economic opportunities in rural areas

questions.explanation: Census data on population size and structure guide planning of schools, hospitals, roads, jobs and revenue allocation.

questions.question: The next best alternative forgone when a choice is made is called ______.
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative you give up. It is the real cost of any choice, measured in forgone options rather than naira.

questions.question: The law of diminishing returns states that as more units of a variable factor are added to a fixed factor, ______.
questions.explanation: With at least one factor fixed, each extra unit of the variable factor eventually adds less to output, so marginal product falls. Total output can still rise, and fixed cost does not change.

questions.question: The owner of a sole proprietorship has ______ liability for the debts of the business.
questions.explanation: A sole proprietor and the business are not separate in law, so the owner is personally liable for all business debts. Limited liability belongs to registered companies.

questions.question: The maximum number of persons allowed in an ordinary partnership under Nigerian law is ______.
questions.explanation: An ordinary partnership must have at least 2 and at most 20 persons. Larger groups must incorporate as a company.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of perfect competition?
questions.explanation: Under perfect competition many firms sell identical products, so no firm can influence price. A single seller, heavy advertising and barriers to entry belong to monopoly or oligopoly.

questions.question: A market structure dominated by a few large firms is called ______.
questions.explanation: Oligopoly is a market with a few large firms whose decisions affect one another. Monopoly has one seller, and monopsony has one buyer.

questions.question: The function of money that allows goods to be valued and compared is ______.
questions.explanation: As a unit of account, money provides a common measure in which prices are expressed, so goods can be compared. A medium of exchange is used to buy and sell.

questions.question: Inflation is best defined as ______.

options.text: a persistent rise in the general price level
a rise in the price of one good
a fall in the value of output
an increase in the money supply

questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level, which reduces the purchasing power of money. A rise in one price is not inflation.

questions.question: The Central Bank of Nigeria acts as lender of last resort to ______.
questions.explanation: When a bank faces a temporary shortage of funds and cannot borrow elsewhere, the CBN can lend to it, which protects the banking system from collapse.

questions.question: Development banks in Nigeria are mainly established to provide ______.
questions.explanation: Development banks such as the Bank of Industry supply medium- and long-term finance for agriculture, industry and infrastructure, which commercial banks are reluctant to fund.

questions.question: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.explanation: A direct tax is levied on the income or wealth of a person and paid directly to government. VAT, import duty and excise duty are indirect taxes on goods and services.

questions.question: Value added tax is an example of ______.
questions.explanation: VAT is charged on goods and services and collected by sellers on behalf of government, so it is an indirect tax. It is also regressive in effect.

questions.question: A budget deficit occurs when ______.
questions.explanation: A deficit means government plans to spend more than it expects to receive, so it must borrow. Revenue exceeding expenditure is a surplus.

questions.question: Utility in economics means the ______.

options.text: satisfaction derived from consuming a commodity

questions.explanation: Utility is the satisfaction a consumer gets from a good, not its physical usefulness. A good can be useful but give little satisfaction, or give satisfaction with little practical use.

questions.question: Total utility is at its maximum when marginal utility is ______.
questions.explanation: As consumption rises, total utility grows while marginal utility falls. When marginal utility reaches zero, total utility stops rising and is at its maximum; a negative marginal utility would reduce it.

questions.question: Consumer surplus is the difference between the price a consumer is willing to pay and ______.
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus measures the gain from paying less than the maximum one was willing to pay. If a buyer would pay N500 and pays N350, the surplus is N150.

questions.question: An indifference curve shows combinations of two goods that give a consumer ______.
questions.explanation: Every point on an indifference curve yields the same level of satisfaction, so the consumer is indifferent between the combinations. Higher curves represent greater satisfaction.

questions.question: Gross domestic product measures the total value of goods and services produced ______.

options.text: by a country’s citizens anywhere in the world
within a country in a year

questions.explanation: GDP counts output produced inside a country’s borders in a year, regardless of the producer’s nationality. Output by citizens abroad belongs to GNP, not GDP.

questions.question: Real gross domestic product is measured at ______.
questions.explanation: Real GDP uses constant base-year prices, so changes reflect actual output rather than inflation. Nominal GDP uses current prices.

questions.question: Per capita income is obtained by dividing national income by ______.
questions.explanation: Per capita income is national income per head of population. It is a rough measure of average living standards and ignores how income is distributed.

questions.question: Transfer payments are excluded from national income because they ______.
questions.explanation: Transfer payments such as pensions and unemployment benefits move income between people without producing new goods or services. Counting them would double-count.
